case_title: BHAGWANI v. THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
aggravating_circumstances: Barbaric and savage manner of committing rape and murder on an 11-year-old girl
mitigating_circumstances: Appellant belongs to a Scheduled Tribes community, no criminal antecedents, no adverse conduct in jail
offence_finally_established: Kidnapping, rape, and murder of an 11-year-old girl
neutral_facts: The accused, along with another individual, attended a ceremony at a house in the evening. The victim, an 11-year-old girl, went missing and was found dead the next morning. The accused and the other individual were present at the ceremony and later visited a local shopkeeper, where they appeared anxious and admitted to having committed a serious act. Their clothes were later seized and examined. Medical evidence indicated the victim was raped and killed. DNA analysis linked the accused and the other individual to the crime scene. The accused had scratch injuries on his body, which were not explained. The trial court convicted both individuals for the offenses, but the Supreme Court upheld the conviction and converted the death sentence to life imprisonment for 30 years without remission.
